column1: # How many outlets stand behind each of nine reported claims that the argument gives as reported, by unnamed people: one row per claim (a to i), made on Nov 25, 2026 from saved pages read whole. For each claim: what is claimed; the first report (outlet, date, how it describes its own sources, saved id); second reports that rest on their OWN sources, each read; relays (how many, with saved ids); any denial or contradiction; a verdict (one outlet, two, three or four with their own sources); pages a search named that could not be saved (leads only, not evidence); a note. Quotations were checked against the saved copies by script. An outlet that repeats another's report is a relay, not a second source; a second outlet with its own unnamed sources is still unnamed sources.

column3: first report: outlet, date, its sourcing in its own words, saved id
column4: independent second reports (own sourcing), each read
column8: not saved (leads only: pages a search named that could not be saved)

column5: 3: Economic Daily News, Taiwan, Jul 24, 2026: "華爾街日報報導" [cn-factions-ding-wsj-relay-20260724]; World Forum reproducing the Journal's Chinese text [cn-ga31-corrob-4]; the Journal's own Chinese edition [man-16164974de2c] (same outlet, text layer broken)

column2: Three bodies (cyberspace regulator, state planner, industry ministry) dissuaded companies from buying the H20 (summer 2025)
column3: Same day, Aug 12, 2025, three outlets with their own people: Bloomberg (on The Business Times): "sources familiar with the matter said, asking not to be named discussing sensitive information" [cn-le11-bbg-h20avoid-bt-20250812]; the same article on Bloomberg Law [cn-ga31-corrob-9]. The three bodies by name: Financial Times, Aug 20, 2025: "According to people with knowledge of the regulatory action, the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology" [man-cn-ft-20250821-regulators]
column4: Financial Times, Aug 12, 2025 (a third-party mirror of the syndicated copy): "said three people familiar with the situation" [cn-le11-ft-h20justify-aggregoctt] (names the industry ministry only); Reuters, Aug 12, 2025, as The Business Standard (tbsnews.net) carried it on Aug 13: "the people, who declined to be identified because the meetings were not public" [ms-bj-20250812-caution-tbs]; Central News Agency's Chinese rendering of the same Reuters report: "這些知情人士因相關會談未對外公開而不願具名" [cn-ga31-carriers2-39]; The Information, Aug 12, 2025 (own sources), held only as others relay it: "兩位知情人士表示，中共監管機構告知，在調查輝達向中國市場銷售的晶片的潛在安全風險之前，必須暫停採購輝達新的晶片" [cn-ga31-carriers2-15]
column5: 3 for The Information's report: Reuters [ms-bj-20250812-caution-tbs], Central News Agency [cn-ga31-carriers2-39], The Epoch Times Hong Kong [cn-ga31-carriers2-15]
column6: Contradiction on the instruction, not on the pressure. Reuters's people: "the companies have not been ordered to stop buying H20 chips" [ms-bj-20250812-caution-tbs]; The Information, by Reuters's relay of it, that the three firms had been ordered by the CAC to suspend Nvidia purchases (see "下令字節跳動、阿里巴巴和騰訊全面暫停購買輝達晶片" [cn-ga31-carriers2-39]).
column7: four outlets with their own sources (Bloomberg, the Financial Times, Reuters, The Information) that the authorities pressed companies against the H20 in August 2025; one outlet (the Financial Times, Aug 20) for the three named bodies and their roles; the outlets disagree on whether firms were told to stop
column9: The argument (point 14) sets Bloomberg, the FT, Reuters and The Information side by side; only the FT names all three bodies.

column2: The cyberspace regulator told ByteDance, Alibaba and others to end testing and orders of the RTX Pro 6000D (Sept 2025)
column3: Financial Times, Sept 17, 2025, hand-saved: "according to three people with knowledge of the matter" [man-cn-ft-20250917-6000d]
column4: Bloomberg, Sept 17, 2025 (Mackenzie Hawkins, Luz Ding; published 20:37 UTC), its own people: "according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the decision isn’t public" [cn-ga31-twelve-2] (names Alibaba only)
column5: 3: Bloomberg's earlier item crediting the FT [cn-ga31-corrob-5]; Bloomberg's corrected relay [cn-against2-ft-all-correction-20250917]; Engadget [ms-bj-20250917-cac-6000d-engadget]
column6: none found. Reuters's report of the day before [cn-labs-rtx6000d-demand-20250916-relay1] gives the firms' own coolness to the card, a cause beside the instruction, not a denial.
column7: two outlets with their own sources (the Financial Times; Bloomberg, later the same day)
column8: Bloomberg's syndication in The Straits Times (a search named its address) credits the FT for the tens of thousands of cards ordered: not saved
column9: Bloomberg's own-sourced article came hours after its relay of the FT; whether its people are different people cannot be known.

column2: Customs teams were mobilised at major ports to check chip shipments (Oct 2025)
column3: Financial Times, Oct 9, 2025, hand-saved: "according to three people with knowledge of the matter" [man-cn-ft-20251009-customs]
column5: 3: OODA Loop [ms-bj-20251009-customs-ooda]; World Journal, Oct 10, 2025: "金融时报引述三位知情人士报导" [cn-ga31-corrob-6]; The Economic Times, Oct 10, 2025, headline and summary only [cn-ga31-corrob-25]
column6: none found (searches of customs.gov.cn and cac.gov.cn for a directive found none)
column8: Reuters's own relay, which says it asked customs and could not verify (a search named its address; the page is not saved): the saved Economic Times copy holds only its headline and summary
column9: The FT's own page dates it Oct 9; some relays give Oct 10.

column2: New data-centre projects that took any state funds must use only home-made AI chips; those under 30% complete to remove foreign chips (Reuters, Nov 5, 2025)
column3: Reuters, Nov 5, 2025, on The Standard: "two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters" [ms-bj-20251105-statefunded-standard]
column4: Earlier, not later: Leiphone, Oct 31, 2025, from a circulating paper it neither shows nor names: "有最新流传的“窗口指导”相关文件写道" [cn-factions-window-guidance-leiphone-20251031]; "有补贴等地方力量参与的项目，应全部使用国产芯片" [cn-factions-window-guidance-leiphone-20251031] (projects in which local forces such as subsidies take part are to use home-made chips only); "可要求对国外芯片进行拆除" [cn-factions-window-guidance-leiphone-20251031] (may be required to remove foreign chips). A second saved copy of the same Leiphone page: [cn-ga31-corrob-34] (not proven the same bytes; both kept).
column7: one outlet (Reuters) for the rule as worded, its scope (any state funds) and its 30% line; an earlier trade-press account (Leiphone) gives a like rule, from a paper of its own, for projects with local subsidies, with removal left open: overlapping, not the same claim
column8: South China Morning Post, Aug 17, 2025, on a share of more than 50% home-made in publicly owned hubs: its site answered 403, not saved; Investing.com's rewrite crediting Reuters: 403
column9: A city's published reply (Pingdingshan, Tier 1) shows one publicly funded centre, planned and approved in 2024, designed, by the reply of June 2025, on 80% or more home-made AI chips: an official text for one project, not the national rule (see OFFICIAL_RECORD.md, section 2.3).

column2: Customs agents were told the H200 is not permitted; companies told to buy only when necessary (January 2026)
column3: Reuters, Jan 14, 2026, on The Standard: "according to three people briefed on the matter" [ms-bj-20260114-customs-h200-standard]; companies "explicitly instructed not to purchase the chips unless necessary, two of the people and a third source said" [ms-bj-20260114-customs-h200-standard]
column4: South China Morning Post, Jan 22, 2026 (Archive capture of that day), its own people, for a hold at the border: "Chinese customs officials are currently holding Nvidia’s H200 chips at the border" [cn-counter-b19-4-wayback], "according to three people familiar with the matter, who declined to be named because of the sensitivity of the issue" [cn-counter-b19-4-wayback]. Later, not within two weeks: Wall Street Journal, Jul 23, 2026: "Beijing told some companies they could buy the H200s only when necessary" [man-cn-factions-wsj-ding]
column5: held relays: Yahoo carrying Reuters [cn-acts-reuters-customs-20260114]; Lianhe Zaobao's mention, Jan 28, 2026: "路透社本月报道，中国海关曾告知代理商，H200晶片不被允许进入中国" [cn-cnpress-zaobao-h200-conditions-20260128]
column6: Asked about a report that the government would approve purchases only in special cases, the commerce ministry, Jan 22, 2026: "我不了解你提到的情况" [cn-ga15-mofcom-presser-20260122] (not a denial)
column7: two outlets with their own sources for the customs side (Reuters: what agents were told; the Post: chips held at the border); one outlet among saved pages within two weeks for "only when necessary" (Reuters); The Information's like report of Jan 13 is held as Reuters's report of Jan 14 relays it [ms-bj-20260114-customs-h200-standard] and as a reporter's question at the commerce ministry
column8: Reuters relaying The Information, Jan 7 and Jan 13, 2026; Reuters relaying the FT, Jan 16 to 17, 2026 (shipments blocked, suppliers paused); Reuters relaying Nikkei Asia, Jan 15, 2026: 403 or refused when fetched, and the Internet Archive has no capture of the Jan 13 and Jan 15 relays on Investing.com (404)
column9: The Post's Jan 22 article is a separate report from the Post's own three people; it is not Reuters's report of Jan 14 carried by the Post.

column2: Beijing approved H200 purchases with conditions for ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent and others (January 2026)
column3: Bloomberg, Jan 8, 2026: "China plans to approve some imports of Nvidia Corp. ’s H200 chips as soon as this quarter, according to people familiar with the situation" [cn-acts-bloomberg-jan8]; Bloomberg, Jan 23, 2026: "Regulators have recently granted in-principle approval for Alibaba, Tencent Holdings Ltd. and ByteDance Ltd. to move to the next stage of preparations for purchases, people familiar with the matter said" [cn-acts-bloomberg-jan23]
column4: Reuters, Jan 28, 2026, on The Standard, its own people: "four people familiar with the matter told Reuters" [ms-bj-20260128-h200-nod-standard], "have been approved to purchase more than 400,000 H200 chips in total" [ms-bj-20260128-h200-nod-standard]; Reuters, Jan 30, 2026 (DeepSeek too): "two people familiar with the matter told Reuters" [cn-acts-reuters-deepseek-20260130]; South China Morning Post, Jan 28, 2026 (updated Jan 29; an Internet Archive capture): "Beijing has begun approving imports of Nvidia’s H200 graphics processing units (GPUs), according to two sources familiar with the matter" [cn-ga31-inte-scmp-h200-approvals-20260128-wayback]; it credits Reuters for the 400,000
column5: 2 held: Central News Agency, Jan 28, 2026: "4名知情人士向路透社透露" [cn-ga31-corrob-36]; Lianhe Zaobao, Jan 28, 2026, relaying Reuters and Bloomberg [cn-cnpress-zaobao-h200-conditions-20260128]
column6: Next day, Nvidia's chief executive (Voice of America's Chinese rendering of his words at Taipei airport, Jan 29, 2026): "我认为中国政府仍在决策中，我们尚未收到采购订单，我们也没有收到新闻报道所说的相关信息" [cn-ga31-counter-40]; the South China Morning Post's English (Archive capture, as above): "I believe the Chinese government is still deciding, we have not received purchase orders" [cn-ga31-inte-scmp-h200-approvals-20260128-wayback]; Bloomberg, as Tom's Hardware carried it: "It’s up to the Chinese government now but they are still deciding" [cn-against2-huang-no-new-orders-20260129]; the foreign ministry, Jan 29, 2026: "具体问题建议向中方主管部门进行询问" [cn-ga31-corrob-23]; the commerce ministry, asked on Mar 19, 2026, said it was not aware [cn-ga15-mofcom-presser-20260319]
column7: three outlets with their own sources that Beijing let the three firms go ahead in principle, with conditions (Bloomberg Jan 23: prepare orders; Reuters Jan 28: approved to buy; the South China Morning Post Jan 28: began approving imports); one outlet (Reuters) for the count of more than 400,000 and for the four companies and the ministries (Jan 30); contradicted the next day by Nvidia's chief executive (still deciding; no purchase orders)
column8: Wall Street Journal, Jan 28, 2026 (wsj.com is a site the project's page saver does not fetch); the South China Morning Post's page itself (403; read in the Archive capture instead)
column9: Bloomberg Jan 23 and Reuters Jan 28 describe different stages (leave to prepare orders; approval to buy); neither is a written approval.

column2: The split inside Beijing: commerce favoured imports, national security-focused officials within the cyberspace regulator and the security ministry pushed home-made chips, and the latter position gained ground (Nov 2026)
column3: Financial Times, Nov 13, 2026 (Eleanor Olcott), hand-saved; the paper's own words: "favoured imports as a way to sustain China’s AI development while domestic semiconductor manufacturers built up their capabilities" [man-e2596eab15f4]; "Over the past year, the latter position has gained ground" [man-e2596eab15f4]; for the planner's lead: "According to people familiar with the matter, the push was led by the National Development and Reform Commission" [man-e2596eab15f4]
column4: none found. The same paper said it earlier (Aug 20, 2025): other departments "such as the commerce and foreign affairs ministries" were more open [man-cn-ft-20250821-regulators]: same outlet.
column5: 1: The Next Web, Nov 14, 2026: "Beijing was also split, according to the paper" [cn-factions-tnw-ft-access]
column9: Kyle Chan's words in the Washington Post (Commentary) are an analyst's reading, not a report of the split; the Wall Street Journal's Chinese edition of Sept 2025 (held only as a reprint with no licence shown, a lead) sets some officials against the industry, a different split.

column2: About 600,000 Nvidia chips (H200s) stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to the mainland (Nov 2026)
column3: Reuters, Nov 5, 2026, on CNA: "About 600,000 of Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to China, two people familiar with the matter said" [cn-clips-evidence-1]
column5: 4: Yahoo carrying Reuters [cn-clips-reuters-hongkong-yahoo]; Data Center Dynamics: "according to a report from Reuters" [sw-datacenterdynamicscom-02]; DigiTimes, Nov 6, 2026 [cn-le12-digitimes-tw-773804-www]; Reuters itself, Nov 18, 2026: "Reuters reported earlier this month that around 600,000 H200 chips were being stored in Hong Kong" [cn-acts-reuters-halt-20261118-relay2]
column6: none; the foreign ministry, asked, Nov 9, 2026: "For anything specific, I’d refer you to competent authorities" [cn-ga31-corrob-22]. A different count, not a contradiction: the FT in August 2026 put Nvidia's stock at about 500,000 H200s, mainly for Chinese buyers, by Central News Agency's rendering: "輝達仍有約50萬顆H200晶片庫存，主要供應中國客戶" [cn-ga31-carriers-26]
column9: Palmer Luckey's 600,000 (clip of Nov 19, 2026) gives no source and matches Reuters's figure; it is not a second report.
